declared_purpose: Provide real-time general and vertical search, parallel batch search, capability discovery, and full-page URL extraction for AI agents. API credentials are optional and provide higher limits (SKILL.md:3-16, 28-30, 97-111).

data_operations.operation: Read and infer local runtime configuration; persist the recommended command
data_operations.data_scope: Platform, runtime availability/version, probe errors and warnings, recommended runtime, and executable/script path
data_operations.condition: Read existing configuration for routine use; detect runtimes when configuration is absent or fails. Installation instructions require recording the recommended runtime locally.

data_operations.operation: Read dotenv files and import their assignments into the process environment
data_operations.source: Startup loaders in all four CLIs
data_operations.data_scope: Every nonempty parsed assignment from scripts/.env and the skill-root .env, including ANYSEARCH_API_KEY
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local CLI process environment; exported values can also reach child processes
data_operations.condition: Files exist. Loading occurs before command dispatch, including offline doc calls and calls supplying a CLI key. This broad import is an implementation choice.

data_operations.operation: Read packaged interface documentation and return it locally
data_operations.condition: doc or an applicable usage/help path runs. These renderers perform local reads; credential loading still occurs at startup.

data_operations.operation: Select the request recipient and attach authentication and client metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Optional API key in Authorization: Bearer; skill version in X-Anysearch-Client; command-specific request data
data_operations.condition: An API command runs. A configured key is attached automatically. Node.js selects its base URL before dotenv loading; Python, PowerShell, and Bash select it afterward. Custom HTTP endpoints are supported by the implementation.

data_operations.operation: Classify query topics and prescribe search coverage
data_operations.data_scope: Query-derived domain categories, capability selection, and domain-specific query reformulations
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Agent routing context; selected categories and reformulations subsequently enter API requests
data_operations.condition: Vertical discovery is explicitly required for domain overlap. Uncertainty prescribes one general plus vertical searches; intersections prescribe rephrasing the same question across domains. This is topic inference, with no implemented personal-profile inference shown.

data_operations.operation: Disclose selected domains and receive capability schemas
data_operations.source: get_sub_domains command and agent caching instruction
data_operations.data_scope: Up to five domain names as repeated domain query parameters; returned capability descriptions and parameter schemas
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GET /v1/sub-domains at the selected API base; results return to the caller and are prescribed to be cached within the agent session
data_operations.condition: Capability discovery is requested or required before vertical search. The discovery request contains domain names rather than the original search text. Session caching is instructed, not implemented as a CLI disk cache.

data_operations.operation: Disclose single or parallel search requests
data_operations.data_scope: Query text; supplied tag, params, zone, language, and max_results. Batch normalization selects these fields rather than forwarding arbitrary top-level item fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: POST /v1/search at the selected API base
data_operations.condition: A valid search is invoked. Batch search issues one independent request per valid item, up to five concurrently. Schema-required parameters are explicitly required; optional parameters may be omitted.

data_operations.operation: Read a caller-selected batch input file
data_operations.data_scope: Entire selected file as text, then parsed or repaired query objects
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local CLI memory; normalized search fields subsequently go to /v1/search
data_operations.condition: The selected batch input starts with @. File reading is an optional input mechanism; it does not itself disclose the complete file remotely.

data_operations.operation: Disclose an extraction URL and receive page content
data_operations.data_scope: Complete supplied URL in a JSON url field; returned page title, source URL, and content
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: POST /v1/extract at the selected API base; formatted content returns to the caller
data_operations.condition: A nonempty URL is provided. The CLI delegates extraction to the API rather than directly fetching the target site. Subsequent backend fetch behavior is unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Return formatted search results and batch query headings
data_operations.data_scope: Result titles, URLs, content or snippets, result count, search duration; batch headings repeat input query text
data_operations.condition: Results are returned. This ordinary tool return establishes no additional remote recipient or durable storage by itself.

data_operations.source: HTTP parsing and single-command error handlers
data_operations.data_scope: Error message and request_id; qualifying error data without field redaction; up to 500 characters of invalid JSON response text
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI stderr/error stream and its caller
data_operations.condition: An API request fails or returns invalid JSON. Batch handlers generally return message/request_id; Python, Node.js, and PowerShell can also carry the invalid-response prefix through their shared error construction.

data_operations.data_scope: Complete per-query response bodies and HTTP status, or synthetic local-error responses
data_operations.condition: Bash batch_search reaches execution. Disk-backed response collection is an implementation choice; other runtimes collect results in memory.

data_operations.operation: Delete the Bash batch temporary directory
data_operations.data_scope: Temporary batch response files and their directory
data_operations.condition: Normal completion, detected formatting failure, or INT/TERM while the cancellation trap remains installed. The trap is removed before output rendering; secure erasure is not established.

data_operations.operation: Register an optional account using an email address
data_operations.source: English and Chinese README registration workflows
data_operations.data_scope: Real reachable email used as account username; response account information and API key
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: POST https://api.anysearch.com/v1/auth/email/register; response returns to the agent
data_operations.condition: The user selects registration rather than anonymous use. Email collection is explicitly required for this chosen account flow, while basic search supports anonymous access.

data_operations.operation: Persist and reuse credentials; communicate account details
data_operations.data_scope: ANYSEARCH_API_KEY; username/email and login_url; newly returned auto_registered key
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local .env for future sessions; user-facing account or approval messages
data_operations.condition: README email registration requires saving the returned key and telling the user their username and login URL. Separately, quota-triggered auto-registration requires explicit approval before saving and retrying. The shared reference additionally says to present the key for approval. These are agent instructions, not automatic CLI save/retry code.

data_operations.operation: Run developer tests through a local HTTP stub and retain test state in memory
data_operations.data_scope: Synthetic queries, URLs, filters, client header, request method/path/body, subprocess environment, and captured stdout/stderr
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port; in-memory STATE.requests and subprocess results; test console on failures
data_operations.condition: The developer test harness is invoked. It removes the inherited ANYSEARCH_API_KEY, sets a loopback base, and launches normal CLIs, whose dotenv loaders remain active. Recorded request fields omit Authorization, although the HTTP receiver can receive that header.

data_operations.operation: Read and optionally rewrite packaged source during generation
data_operations.data_scope: Skill version, shared constants, CLI source, generated constants, and documentation-rendering blocks
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory and the four CLI source files
data_operations.condition: The generator is invoked. Changed files are written unless --check is used; this is a development path.

data_operations.data_scope: Selected release archive/tag and optional requests dependency
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GitHub for the documented archive download; local archive and skill directory; dependency resolver destination is unspecified
data_operations.condition: Manual download installation or Python dependency installation is selected.

data_operations.data_scope: Vulnerability description, reproduction steps, potential impact, and optional suggested fix
data_operations.condition: Someone chooses the separate vulnerability-reporting workflow; no automatic reporting mechanism is packaged.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated dotenv assignments and credential reads during offline doc calls or explicitly keyed calls
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI process environment and inherited child-process environments
potential_excess.condition: A dotenv file exists; unrelated nonempty assignments are imported, even before commands that do not need credentials.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Credential lookup supports optional authenticated search. Importing every assignment is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve the selected API key with the documented priority and preserve deliberately configured endpoint behavior.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: For extra data, allowlist supported configuration names instead of importing arbitrary assignments. For redundant reads, defer credential loading until an API command needs it and skip key lookup when an explicit key already resolves authentication.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep anonymous use, documented key priority, intentional endpoint configuration, and offline documentation rendering working.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unfiltered error data and invalid-response prefixes, potentially including returned credentials or account information
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI stderr/error stream and its caller; no additional remote recipient is established
potential_excess.condition: An error contains data or an invalid response contains sensitive text. Actual sensitive contents depend on the API response.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Failure diagnosis requires actionable error information, not necessarily the complete error payload.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report the failure, useful validation/quota details, and request_id; signal when a replacement key is available.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Allowlist diagnostic fields, redact credentials, and omit raw response prefixes by default. This narrows output data within required error reporting.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain information needed for argument recovery, quota handling, and approved key-saving flows without printing key values.

potential_excess.data_scope: The newly returned auto_registered API key
potential_excess.condition: The agent follows the shared reference instruction to present the key for approval after a rate-limit response.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Approval concerns saving a credential for future use. SKILL.md already supplies a consent prompt that does not expose the credential.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Notify the user that a new key arrived, request approval to save it, and disclose its storage location and reuse.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Present the key's availability rather than its value. Keep the credential within the response-handling and approved local-storage path.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve explicit confirmation before saving and the prescribed retry after approval.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete batch response envelopes, including fields unused by the output formatter
potential_excess.condition: Bash batch_search executes; responses are written to disk before formatting.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Parallel search requires collecting and ordering results, but does not inherently require durable filesystem writes.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve concurrent requests, input ordering, formatted results, and independent failure reporting.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Avoid the redundant persistence action by collecting responses in memory. If temporary files remain necessary, store only formatted results or allowlisted error fields and keep cleanup installed through rendering.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain partial-success behavior and remove temporary files on normal completion and covered failures; do not discard result content needed by the caller.

potential_excess.data_scope: A real ANYSEARCH_API_KEY loaded from local dotenv files during developer tests
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The loopback HTTP stub; for Python, PowerShell, and Bash, a dotenv ANYSEARCH_API_BASE_URL can instead select another endpoint
potential_excess.condition: The test harness runs in an installation containing such dotenv assignments. Clearing the inherited key does not prevent the child CLI from reloading it.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The tests exercise synthetic HTTP contracts and do not require a real account credential.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Send synthetic search/extraction requests to the local stub and verify formatting, routing, concurrency, and errors.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Isolate test configuration from user dotenv files, pin the loopback endpoint after configuration loading, and use a synthetic credential only for explicit authentication tests. This removes extra credential data from required test requests.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep normal production dotenv behavior unchanged and preserve all local contract assertions.

unknowns: Provider retention, logging, tracking, credential handling, downstream recipients, and deletion are unresolved. SKILL.md:87 reports provider claims; backend source is absent and SECURITY.md:33-36 excludes the backend and consuming platforms.
The extraction backend's target-site requests, redirects, caches, and handling of URL credentials or query parameters are not supplied.
Caller/platform storage of tool arguments, stdout, stderr, chat, and returned credentials is unknown. Ordinary CLI returns alone do not establish remote disclosure or persistence.
Actual dotenv contents, custom endpoints, user queries, and returned payloads are unavailable. Sensitive-content disclosure and test rerouting remain conditional.

The actual auto_registered response schema, account-creation behavior, and agent enforcement of approval/save/retry instructions are unresolved. The supplied CLIs do not implement those agent workflows.
No credential-file permissions, retention deadline, revocation workflow, or deletion mechanism is specified. Gitignore entries do not establish access control.
Temporary-file cleanup after abrupt termination or failure outside the covered paths is unresolved; filesystem removal does not establish secure erasure.

The operational necessity of the client-version header and the task-specific necessity of hybrid fan-out, particular URL components, optional parameters, and result counts cannot be established from source alone.
Dependency-library transport behavior and dependency-download destinations are not fully supplied.
